comparisons.peer_summary: Investment banking revenues were $7.74 billion in 2024, up 24% from 2023, primarily due to significantly higher revenues in debt underwriting (leveraged finance) and equity underwriting (secondary and IPOs), as well as higher advisory revenues from increased M&A activity.
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup and Goldman Sachs both disclose substantial growth in investment banking revenues for 2024, driven by a recovery in underwriting activities. Citigroup reports a 38% increase in Investment Banking revenues due to a 'rebound in overall wallet activity,' while Goldman Sachs reports a 24% increase, primarily reflecting 'significantly higher revenues in debt underwriting, primarily driven by leveraged finance activity, and in equity underwriting.' Both firms point to the resurgence in leveraged finance and IPOs as key growth engines.

comparisons.peer_summary: Banking & Payments revenue was $35.3 billion, up 11%, driven by Investment Banking fees up 37% (ranked #1 globally), Payments revenue up 1% despite margin compression from higher rates, and Lending revenue up 8% due to higher rates and the First Republic acquisition.
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase both report strong growth in Investment Banking revenues for 2024, attributed to favorable market conditions and increased transaction volumes. Citigroup’s Investment Banking revenues increased 38% due to a 'rebound in overall wallet activity,' while JPMorgan’s Investment Banking revenue increased 36% (fees up 37%), driven by 'higher fees across products' and specifically noting 'wallet share gains in IPOs.' Both disclosures highlight the recovery in M&A and underwriting pipelines.

comparisons.comparison: Citigroup and Morgan Stanley both disclose significant growth in investment banking revenues for 2024, driven by the recovery in M&A and underwriting. Citigroup’s Investment Banking revenues increased 38% due to a 'rebound in overall wallet activity,' while Morgan Stanley’s investment banking net revenues increased 35%, reflecting 'an increase in underwriting and Advisory revenues' with higher completed M&A transactions. Both firms experienced double-digit growth in this segment, reflecting industry-wide recovery.
